  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="roles-map-title">What is each piece for?</h2>
  <p>The course combines formative activities and assessed deliverables. They support each other, but they do not play the same role.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="course-flow">
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">1</span><h3>Adventures</h3><p>Guided in-class work. Adventures establish the context, data and technical skills.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">2</span><h3>Mini-tests and exercises</h3><p>Consolidation. They help check readings, practise and vary datasets.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">3</span><h3>Challenges</h3><p>Short deliverables. They extend the module adventure with more autonomy.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">4</span><h3>Poster</h3><p>Communication. The poster turns an analysis into a clear visual message for a broad audience.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">5</span><h3>Exam and project</h3><p>Integration. The exam checks individual autonomy; the project checks a complete team workflow.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="path-title">

  <div class="course-flow">
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">01</span>
  <h3>Prepare</h3>

  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">03</span>

  <span class="flow-number">04</span>

  <span class="flow-number">05</span>

  <h3>Challenges</h3>

  <p>Expected product: a short, readable, rendered or verifiable deliverable linked to the module.</p>

  </div>
  </article>

  <p>Communicate a story from real data as an A1 poster, with a clear question, cited sources, relevant graphics and a repository structured from the Quarto template.</p>
  <p>Expected product: a GitHub repository containing the poster and the elements needed to understand the team work.</p>
  <div class="resource-link-list">

  <h3>Exam</h3>
  <p>Work independently in an applied situation and show reasonable autonomy with R, Quarto and data.</p>
  <p>Expected product: a completed Quarto report that renders, is interpreted and matches the mission.</p>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="criteria-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="criteria-title">Cross-cutting criteria</h2>
  <p>These criteria come back in challenges, the exam and the project. They explain what is valued beyond the exact format of each submission.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="reading-map">
  <article><h3>Verifiable work</h3><p>The file, render or repository makes it possible to see what was done and rerun the essential steps.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Readable code</h3><p>Objects have clear names, transformations are structured and unnecessary code is removed.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Justified choices</h3><p>Filters, recoding choices, graphs and summaries are linked to the question rather than added by reflex.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Careful interpretation</h3><p>Conclusions state what the data support, without going beyond what is observed.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Communication</h3><p>The deliverable is understandable for someone who does not see you working.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Following instructions</h3><p>The right file is submitted, in the right place, with the requested elements and without unnecessary files.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section resource-split" aria-labelledby="instructions-title">
  <div>
  <h2 id="instructions-title">Read instructions without mixing them up</h2>
  <p>Assessments use several supports. Distinguishing them helps avoid submission errors and misunderstandings about what is expected.</p>
  <ol class="clean-steps">
  <li>Read the course site page to understand the pedagogical role of the assessment.</li>
  <li>Check Brio for dates, official submission, weights and administrative adjustments.</li>
  <li>Use the template repository only as a technical starting point, not as a replacement for instructions.</li>
  <li>Compare your final product with the instructions before submitting.</li>
  </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-compact-list" aria-label="Sources to distinguish">
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Course site</h3><p>Explains the path, pedagogical expectations and useful links.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Brio</h3><p>Confirms official requirements for the session.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>GitHub repository</h3><p>Provides a work structure and starting files.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Feedback</h3><p>Indicates what to reuse in the next product.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section resource-split" aria-labelledby="official-title">
  <div>
  <h2 id="official-title">Official reference</h2>
  <p>The course site explains the pedagogical logic of assessments. Brio remains the official source for dates, submission files, weights and administrative details. If there is a contradiction, the official instruction posted on Brio or given in class for the current session prevails.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-compact-list" aria-label="Preparing a submission">
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Before starting</h3><p>Identify the expected product, data, format and submission location.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>While working</h3><p>Build a simple version that works, then improve clarity and explanations.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Before submitting</h3><p>Render the document, check outputs, reread the interpretation and remove unnecessary files.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>After feedback</h3><p>Keep useful corrections and reuse them in the next challenge, exam or project.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>
